company.mission:
# Swift Arrival autonomous playability frontier

Turn the private Swift Arrival network-interaction prototype at
/company/projects/swift-arrival into a genuinely playable compact vertical slice. The founder has
reported only that horizontal movement feels reversed relative to the view and apparently solid truck
geometry does not behave like real collision geometry. Treat those as evidence, not a decomposed
backlog. Diagnose and prioritise the highest-leverage experience problems from the game, executable
checks and independent playtests.

Exec must appoint one accountable non-producing Game Product lead and return immediately to portfolio
availability. The lead remains a supervisor: it judges priorities, commissions bounded attributed
Staff Work, inspects exact native outcomes, redirects mistakes and accepts only clean candidates. One
end-to-end gameplay Staff worker is the default. Add a specialist only after recording a stable seam
whose independent value repays coordination cost. Staff owns every source, test, evidence and commit
change.

Use event-driven cycles only: new candidate evidence can trigger independent playtesting, and a new
playtest result can trigger lead judgement. Do not use cron, heartbeat, a recurring keep-working
prompt, a manufactured task count or content expansion as progress. No new evidence may correctly
produce quiet. Deterministic probes prove mechanics, not feel. Independent playtest evidence is
untrusted material for the lead, not an implementation command, and never replaces founder taste.

The playable slice must provide view-relative first-person movement and driving; real physical
boundaries rather than clamp-only collision illusions; coherent mouse look and blocked movement;
legible pickup, drop, seat and unload feedback; host-authoritative shared player, vehicle, cargo and
delivery state; recovery from ordinary mistakes without a soft lock; honest presentation; and clean
positive and negative multiplayer probes. Preserve original placeholder assets and the bounded local
route. Do not add broad content until these foundations are true.

All work is local and private. Do not publish, deploy, purchase, contact anyone, use unlicensed or
third-party assets, exercise external effects or promote experimental commits into the source
Dogfood 4 company. Stop only for a stable authority, infrastructure or product-direction blocker, the
spend ceiling, or a prepared exact founder review target.

work.title: Make the playable core real: view-relative movement, solid collision, recoverable crate
work.outcome:
The founder's two reports - sideways movement feeling reversed and the solid-looking truck not stopping anyone - share one root: the prototype has no physics at all. The player is moved numerically on fixed truck axes while the camera is locked facing the cab, and nothing in the world has a collision shape. This work makes first-person movement follow the view with real mouse look, gives the truck and world real collision the player can walk in, and guarantees a dropped crate can always be picked back up, so an ordinary mistake can never soft-lock the delivery.

Exact contract. Repo slug swift-arrival (checked out at /company/projects/swift-arrival), from baseline commit 84ff1745b29267708599e94036ec6f7a2a7e0457 (tree 25733ead6eb7c83221048d323838a5cadc2a235e). Preserve the original placeholder assets and labels, the bounded truck route (z 0..40) and destination zone, the ENet host-authoritative model, and the scripted-probe discipline. No content broadening, no third-party assets, no external effects.

Diagnosis to build against, verified in baseline main.gd:
- Strafe inversion and no look: _apply_player_move adds raw truck-local Vector3(mv.x,0,mv.y) while the camera always faces truck-local +Z, so D moves toward camera-left; there is no mouse look at all.
- Clamp-only collision: every object is a MeshInstance3D; the player is clamped to the truck interior (x -1..1, z -3.3..3.3) with one special-cased doorway rule; the player can never leave the truck; the truck drives through a dropped crate.
- Unrecoverable drop: _request_release teleports the crate to world z = truck_z - 5 no matter where the player stands. Hands cannot reach below truck_z - 2.85 and the grab limit is 1.6 m, so a release at route start (truck_z = 0, and the truck cannot reverse below 0) is permanently unrecoverable. This is the owner-observed intermittent failure.

Required result, one candidate commit:
1. View-relative first-person movement: strafe and forward follow the camera basis; mouse-look yaw rotates the view and the movement basis; turning while blocked stays coherent (no wall pass-through while turning).
2. Real collision boundaries replacing clamps: solid truck and world geometry blocks the player from both sides (for example CharacterBody3D move_and_slide against StaticBody3D), the player can leave the truck and walk the bounded area on the ground, the crate is a physical object that rests on geometry, and the truck cannot drive through a dropped crate.
3. Recoverable crate handling: release places the crate relative to the player's actual position and facing, and every dropped crate in the bounded area remains pick-up-able, including behind the truck at route start; no reachable state requires a restart.
4. Host-authoritative shared player, vehicle, cargo and delivery state: clients request, the host validates and resolves (including player movement validity, not just interactions), and joining clients receive coherent state.
5. Legible feedback for pickup, drop, seat and unload: distinct visible cues plus the HUD log; rejections (grab refused, seat occupied) are visible to the requester.
6. Honest presentation: controls shown match reality; nothing is labeled physical that is not.

Probe contract - probes assert observed state and exit nonzero when the mechanic is broken; a printed PASS without an assertion is not acceptance. These four commands are the acceptance gates, declared atomically with this Work and run in the Attempt workspace:
- sh run-probe.sh HOSTLOG CLIENTLOG - positive delivery loop green end-to-end (join, pickup, seat, drive bounded route, unload in zone, host-authoritative completion visible on both, clean shutdown).
- sh run-probe.sh --negative HOSTLOG CLIENTLOG - release outside the zone is rejected by the host, delivery does not complete, both processes log PASS (the baseline host-side negative shutdown was declared not acceptance evidence; finish it).
- sh run-probe.sh --mechanics HOSTLOG CLIENTLOG - asserts the movement basis follows view yaw (at a set yaw, strafe displaces the player along camera right, not a fixed world axis) and that closed solid geometry blocks movement (near-zero displacement into a wall).
- sh run-probe.sh --recovery HOSTLOG CLIENTLOG - asserts a crate released behind the truck at route start is recovered and the delivery still completes.

Evidence to preserve and link as artifacts:
- Headless logs of all four probe modes from the accepted candidate.
- One native OS-input playtest bundle under /company/outputs/exp11/playtests/RUNID/ (input trace, host and client logs, screenshots, result) including at least one deliberate mistake and its recovery. Native feel evidence is material for lead judgement, not a gate.
- A plain summary of what changed, what was verified, and known limits; say plainly what was not done. Keep it compact: one focused candidate beats many passes; about 50 USD remains for the whole slice.

work.outcome:

Before inspecting the producer's playtest bundle or implementation details, launch a fresh native host and client using the candidate's own documented surfaces and attempt the bounded route as a new player. Make the live objective, destination/interaction affordance, and seat-exit state legible in the rendered first-person view; debug/event text must not materially cover normal play. Preserve the bounded local route, original placeholder assets, host-authoritative player/vehicle/cargo/delivery state, view-relative movement, real physical boundaries, deliberate-drop recovery, and positive/negative multiplayer semantics. Do not broaden content, publish, deploy, or use external effects.

Commit all source/test/evidence changes as one candidate descended from a1d96fe4ce7280501f3d193fc3c3058a23e8a914. Run the declared gates and the documented player-like rendered X11 lane from pickup through deliberate drop/re-pickup, driving, seat exit, post-exit movement, and successful unload; preserve timestamped input trace, host/client logs, and strongest screenshots for exit and delivery.
